It's sad that the facility you came from didn't have a better re-entry program. As a disclaimer, I work in corrections as an officer at a level 1 and 2 facility but in my state at least we have a slew of re-entry program options available including a work release unit where offenders with less than a year left of their sentence get to go get a real job in the community. Most work at factories and restaurants, and like 30% of their check is automatically taken out and put into a trust so that once they're released they can go get an apartment or house with the saved money and continue their work at the place we got them signed on up at. It's worked pretty damn well for rehabilitation and getting people a job. It's been good for our facility and good for the offenders who have partook in the program. I'd like to see more places do it.

Anyway, the above doesn't help you now. So what to do? Honestly, the best thing you can do now that you're free is be as frugal as possible until things start getting better. Being locked up for almost ten years you should be use to a pretty moderate and mild standard of living in regards to minimalism. I'm not saying don't treat yourself, but understand that trying to keep up with what other people have isn't a worthy venture. Only look at others to make sure they have enough, and not see if they have more than you, if that makes sense. :)

You said in another comment you passed up a work program in prison as you were currently painting a large mural. Is it at all possible that they (The prison) could send you a photo of the work you did? I know there are people and businesses that pay for such things, and if you could showcase your work (which may be limited to what was done while in prison) then you'd be set. I have a buddy who painted a large two story tall mural for the local city showcasing some history stuff and did pretty well for himself on it... it takes a lot of time and skill to complete such things, as you know, so the reward for finding paying gigs for that can be high.

Another thing to consider is the importance of always be looking for work even when you have work. If you're only bringing in $200/WK, I'd be filling in applications for other jobs as often as possible. Lot of high paying unskilled labor jobs that will hire people with a criminal history, most people don't care about that. Construction, even as a general laborer (think getting materials for people, pushing a wheelbarrow around, shovling, etc) do pretty well. Working in a factory is something I did for years, it's easy and mind numbing work. Lot of time to think and plan for your future while you're doing tasks based on muscle memory, and the money isn't usually bad. Working in a warehouse... see if there is like an Amazon warehouse near you. There is one about an hour from here and I hear they pay pretty well. A buddy who has been arrested a few times in the past works there and doesn't completely hate it.

I think the best thing in your situation is finding a consistent job if possible, something with a consistent schedule. That way you have a clear and defined time 'off' of work that you can use to promote a side business doing art for others. You can just let people know you work M-F and are available after 5PM and on the weekends for additional work, etc.

Keep your head up man and understand your situation isn't different from millions of others. Everyone has to find a way to make ends meet and I'm certain you'll come up with something. I personally think all drugs should be decriminalized and regulated, so I don't give a shit that you used to do that in the past and I think it's silly we lock people up for it but unfortunately life is a game and that's currently one of the rules. :(

Good luck to ya man.
